speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is HDB’s approach to assist flat dwellers who experience persistent external wall seepages and ceiling leakages; and (b) whether HDB invests in new capabilities and technologies to tackle long-standing and recurring cases where the HDB maintenance contractors are unable or incapable of rectifying.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether HDB will consider rolling out a national programme of facade repair for ageing HDB blocks in view of the recent spates of external wall seepage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap have raised questions about external water seepages and ceiling leakages.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Desmond Choo also had a question about how MND can support Town Councils with water seepages and wear and tear problems at common areas, which my colleague, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will address separately.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The external walls of HDB blocks are common property under the Town Councils' management and maintenance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As they are subject to wear and tear over time, Town Councils are advised to keep them in good condition by carrying out regular maintenance and repairs where needed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Residents who encounter water seepage through their walls typically report such cases to their Town Council.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The objective is to improve public safety, by facilitating the early detection of potential issues and the timely repair of façades.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ceiling leaks that occur in HDB flats are generally a result of wear and tear over time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In such cases, the responsibility for repairs is shared jointly between the upper and lower floor flat owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Both upper and lower floor flat owners would need to jointly investigate and carry out the repairs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In most cases, leakages can be amicably resolved when flat owners exercise mutual understanding and cooperate with one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: HDB also offers assistance to help upper and lower floor owners resolve ceiling leak issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In cases where the leak is caused by wear and tear, HDB may offer assistance with repairs and co-share the cost of repairs under the Goodwill Repair Assistance (GRA) scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The remaining 50% is then shared equally between the upper and lower floor flat owners.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, if the cause of the leak at the lower floor flat is due to renovations carried out at the upper floor flat, the upper floor flat owner would be fully responsible for rectifying the leak and bearing the full repair cost.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: HDB has been exploring new technologies to improve on current repair methods for ceiling leaks and has identified two new repair methods.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These technologies provide alternative repair options for residents who do not wish to hack their toilet tiles or who prefer to keep the existing finishes in their toilets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For complex and recurring issues which contractors are unable to rectify, HDB will also assist in the investigation and provide advice where possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Lastly, ceiling leaks can also occur for units that are on the top floor, as water seeps into the flat through the roof.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As the roof is part of common property, the Town Council is responsible for addressing the leak.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Where necessary, HDB can provide technical advice to the Town Council on the root cause of the leak and on the appropriate repair methods.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Just to let him know that I have received more than hundred feedback over the last two, three months.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And some very serious cases where water flows out like a tap from the wall.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Town Council contractors will always be called upon to do the repair and they will use a trial-and-error method because they cannot really identify where the source of the seepage is.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And it may not be fixed in one day, they will come another day; and sometimes, it takes multiple sessions to get it done.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It causes a lot of frustrations to residents and also the resources of the contractors as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask and appeal to MND and HDB to intervene in this situation because this is really a basic liveability issue, especially first thing for those that are perennial cases, where HDB should step in?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Because some of these are due to certain batches of HDB flats that were built using a particular technique, prefabrication techniques and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Therefore, the water seepage has been there for many years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I hope the HDB can come in for those cases to help identify the root cause of the problem, use technology like the Minister of State mentioned, use the research that HDB has.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It does help to assist the contractors to tackle the problem as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: This is actually for the good of construction productivity because the contractors will then know how to tackle this problem as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I hope that HDB sees some ownership in this problem as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Because these 30-year-old flats are going to be around for another 30 years, the next 30-year life cycle.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We need to help fix those problems so that they do not face this problem the next 30 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Certainly, we will look at how we can improve rectifying; and also help other organisations, even the contractors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are looking at the building industry, how we can use research and technology to repair and to produce materials and products which are long-lasting and able to rectify such seepages and other kind of defects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is something that we will take note of.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As the cases that the Member has raised may be specific to certain types of construction method, I will take it back and see how we can address the situation together.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As the Minister of State mentioned earlier, it is co-sharing between Town Council and HDB.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: But I believe that more thorough work to be done for the facade repairs under a national programme would be more beneficial in the long run.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: During the inspection, if we see there are things that need to be rectified, we can do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, essentially, we want to see how, as a whole, in Singapore, we can try to inspect and maintain over time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, this is something that we are committed to doing with the Town Council.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We hope, as a whole, in the whole building industry and construction industry, we want to see how we can enhance, not only the maintainability of the building but, in particular, also the facade.
